issues.title: Exact BF for sparse perfect hash joins, filled from the perfect-HT slot bitmap
issues.hypothesis: In q07 (187ms, 6.2% of total) the lineitem scan emits 18.23M rows, and its only dynamic filter is `optional: l_suppkey>=3 AND <=99999`. The l_suppkey=s_suppkey HASH_JOIN then drops them to 1.46M (8%), costing 0.19s CPU plus a 0.025s projection (warm JSON profile, .dbe/scratch_q07.json). The build has 8016 supplier keys in a 100k range, so it takes the perfect HJ path (range <= MAX_BUILD_SIZE 1M). JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:946) returns false for every perfect hashtable, on the reasoning that 'with a perfect hashtable we expect good min/max pruning'. That only holds for dense builds. Region- or nation-filtered dimension tables (supplier, customer, part under 1M range) are sparse, so min/max prunes nothing. A prior run tried a BF on sparse perfect HJ (q21) and found that rows dropped 37.9M->2.7M but scan CPU rose. That was before two things landed: the exact bitmap BF for small ranges (E0022), whose probe costs about half a hashed one, and the per-value BitPacking select (E0027), which makes the non-filter columns (here l_orderkey, l_extendedprice, l_discount) cost proportional to selectivity. Until E0027 they were fully decoded and then sliced. The perfect HT already holds an exact bitmap of the build keys, bitmap_build_idx (slot = key - build_min), so filling the BF costs a word copy instead of a pass over the HT.
issues.plan: 1) In JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp ~938), stop rejecting a perfect hashtable outright. Allow it when it is sparse: ht->Count() * 4 <= range + 1. Add a parameter, or let the caller compute it, using perfect_join_statistics.build_range or max-min. 2) In FinalizeFilters (~1163), for the perfect case on the no-cast, no-offset path: call TrySetExactBloomFilter(*ht, op, min_val, max_val). The range is < 1M, so the small-range floor always makes it exact. Then add the entry to deferred_bloom_filters as today, but do NOT call ht->SetBuildBloomFilter for the HT finalize, which never runs for a perfect HJ. If the BF did not become exact, skip it. 3) Add PerfectHashJoinExecutor::FillExactBloomFilter(BloomFilter &bf) in perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp/.hpp. It calls bf.Initialize(context, count). It needs exact_min == build_min widened the same way TrySetExactBloomFilter widens it (int64 for signed types) and exact_range == build_range; assert both. It then copies the bitmap_build_idx words into the bf words. Both use 64-bit LSB-first words with bit i == slot i, so bloom_filter.hpp needs an accessor or a friend for the raw word pointer. If bitmap_build_idx.AllValid() (no data pointer), set all bits, or just skip the BF because that case is dense. 4) Push the deferred BFs right after the perfect build is final, through PushBloomFilter. This happens in two places. The serial path is PhysicalHashJoin::Finalize after FinalizeFilters (~1299), when use_perfect_hash is true. The parallel path is PerfectHashJoinBuildEvent::FinishEvent (~656), after FinishBuild returns true. If use_perfect_hash turns out false (duplicates), keep today's behaviour: the regular HT finalize builds and pushes the BF. Make sure the deferred list is not pushed twice and that the BF is not left half-initialized for the fallback. 5) Verify. Check that the q07 lineitem scan shows `l_suppkey IN BF(s_suppkey)` and that its output cardinality drops from 18.2M to ~1.5M, and that results match. Run a micro A/B on q07 hot (3x each). Also check a RIGHT perfect join (q13 customer, dense) and confirm it still gets no BF, because of the density gate.
issues.expected_gain: q07 -8..-15%: about 0.2s CPU of ~1.5s saved in HJ probe and projection, offset by an exact BF probe on 18M rows. Possibly also q02 (ps_suppkey = region-filtered supplier) and q08 (supplier/customer sides). Hidden templates with nation- or region-filtered supplier/customer builds probing lineitem/orders/partsupp (q20, q21-like) should gain too.
issues.generality: Any equi-join whose build is a selective dimension subset with a key range under 1M (perfect HJ), probing a large fact table. This is very common: star joins with region/nation/category filters. Queries where the BF is unselective are protected by the 25% density gate and SelectivityOptionalFilter's runtime auto-disable. Possible slowdown: a probe scan whose BF check costs more than the perfect-HT probe it replaces, which can happen when there are few extra columns and selectivity is moderate (~20%).
issues.risk: Low-medium. The bitmap copy must use exactly the same min and widening as the BF lookup; a mismatch gives wrong results, so test with negative or offset key ranges (e.g. a join on s_suppkey - 50000) and compare against `+0` variants. The fallback-to-regular-HJ path (duplicates) must not push a BF that was never filled.

- gen2 r7: E0023 ANTI deliminator ACCEPTED (q22 -22..-29%).
- gen2 r8: E0024 parallel perfect-HJ build + INNER dense <=4M ACCEPTED (q14 -7%).

- gen2 r11: E0027 = per-value BitPacking select + E0025 tier ACCEPTED (geomean -9.0%; q05/q08/q09/q14/q19 beyond noise). Best 1.676x.

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs BOTH: some template faster beyond its noise AND a visible geomean that improves. Any template slower beyond its noise gets the issue retired.
- Bundle a near-miss with a general second mechanism that hits the SAME template.
- Ideas retired before E0027 (BitPacking select) may be worth retrying. Pre-E0027, any filter that cut scan rows still paid the full decode of the non-filter columns. Sparse-perfect-HJ BF (r12) is the first such retry.

## Key finding r12: perfect HJ never pushes a BF
- CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:946) returns false if is_perfect_hashtable. Perfect HJ applies to any range <=1M (MAX_BUILD_SIZE), or <=4M if density >=1/2 (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:111-122).
- q07: supplier build of 8016 keys in a 100k range, so the lineitem scan emits 18.2M rows (min/max only), the HJ cuts them to 1.46M, and the HJ costs 0.19s CPU.
- The perfect HT has bitmap_build_idx (slot = key - min), which can be copied straight into an exact BF (bloom_filter.hpp: 64-bit LSB-first words, bit = key - exact_min). The deferred BF push normally happens in HashJoinFinalizeEvent::FinishEvent, which never runs for a perfect HJ. The perfect paths are PhysicalHashJoin::Finalize ~1282-1300 (serial) and PerfectHashJoinBuildEvent::FinishEvent ~648 (parallel).
- My attempt to A/B this through SQL (a union with a fake out-of-range supplier row, to force a regular HJ) failed: the fake row did not change the min/max (99999), so it is unclear whether that variant got a BF at all. Wall time was the same.
- If r12 fails: check whether the BF was pushed (scan Dynamic Filters), the scan CPU before and after, and whether SelectivityOptionalFilter disabled it.

## Key finding r11 (landed E0027): BitPacking select
- bitpacking.cpp now has a select callback: per-value FOR extraction when <=1/4 of rows pass. Open follow-ups: the 1/4 threshold is untuned; at 5% pass the select still costs ~50ms over count(*) on 5 cols (~26ns/value, which looks high, worth a perf look); Roaring validity and ALP/Chimp have no select.
- TEMP tables are never compressed. To test compressed storage: ATTACH a file db READ_WRITE + SET force_compression + CHECKPOINT.

## Key finding r9: an exact bitmap BF probe is ~2x cheaper than a hashed BF probe

## Large perfect HA (E0009/E0013): q13 -20% real but q18 +8% beyond noise each time
- Possible cause: 22-bit per-thread tables (~64MB x 8). A retry needs range-sized tables. Unverified.

## Measured (warm JSON)
- q03 (r12): HJ l_orderkey=o_orderkey 0.34s CPU (build 1.45M orders, probe only 301k lineitem after exact BF!), lineitem scan 0.39s (60M -> 301k), orders scan 0.13s, HJ o_custkey 0.12s, agg 0.05s. The HJ build of 1.45M is the cost; the probe is tiny. Idea: when the BF shows that the probe is much smaller than the build... (no mechanism yet).
- q07 (r12): lineitem scan 0.55s, HJ l_suppkey 0.19s, HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 0.29s (build 1.46M lineitem side, probe orders 100k), orders scan 0.12s.
- q09 (r11): lineitem scan 3.8s CPU cold; HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 1.05s warm (build 3.27M lineitem side).
- q13: inner agg 2.02s CPU (15.3M rows, 1.5M groups), orders scan 1.70s (NOT LIKE), decompress proj 0.24s, RIGHT HJ 0.25s.
- q05: lineitem scan 0.93s, HJ l_orderkey 0.33s, multi-key HJ (nationkey+suppkey) 0.15s with an unfiltered supplier build (no BF possible).
- No PK/UNIQUE constraints in the schema.

## How to get full operator timings
- dbe-tool sql "<q>; <q>; SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/scratch_x.json'; <q>", then Grep '"operator_timing"|"operator_name"|"operator_cardinality"|Dynamic Filters|"Conditions"'. /tmp is NOT readable.
- Micro A/B: CREATE TEMP VIEW a/b, then `from a; from b;` alternated 4x in one call. The first run is ~3x slower.
- dbe-tool bash: no pipes.

## Measurement lessons
- Alternate A/B/A/B. Do NOT wrap in count(*) (it changes the plan).
- Bench noise ±10-20% per template. Thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20.3%, q04 ~20%.

## Profile snapshot (r12): q18 544, q13 511, q09 429, q05 203, q07 187, q03 174, q16 170, q08 162, q04 153, q14 118, q17 113, q22 106, q19 95, q02 60. Geomean 175.6.

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation, fused hashed BF probe.
- q18: the 15M-group agg dominates (exhausted).

## Next candidates
1. (dispatched r12) sparse perfect-HJ exact BF.
2. Optimize the BitPacking per-value select loop (26ns/value looks high); tune the 1/4 threshold.
3. q13 agg 127ns/row: range-sized perfect HA, allocated so q18 is not hit.
4. q03/q07/q09: the o_orderkey HJ builds on the large side (1.45M-3.27M) while the BF-filtered probe is small. Look at build/probe side choice after filters.
5. MARK delim joins (IN/EXISTS in OR) via the deliminator.

## Codebase facts
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. Rule order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp.
- Deliminator: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp. Join filters: JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters; build_side_has_filter = IsFiltering(children[1]) (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:210,334).
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp (CanDoPerfectHashJoin :66, BuildPerfectHashTable :144, FinishBuild :262). Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp. FSST: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp. BF: src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp; exact tiers in physical_hash_join.cpp TrySetExactBloomFilter ~972; exact BF fill in join_hashtable.cpp ~731-796.
- BitPacking: src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory, the ledger tail and the profile head, profile 1-2 queries, then dispatch.
